routes.name: Residence Permit on the basis of Self-Employment
Free movement of EU and EEA nationals (Registration Certificate and eResidence Document)

note: Malta, read on Identità's Expatriates Unit pages (identita.gov.mt) on 2026-10-30. The Single Permit (Subsidiary Legislation 217.17) lets a third-country national reside and take up employment for over six months with the employer named only (work for the sponsor); the employer applies through the Single Permit Online Portal while the worker is abroad or legally in Malta or another Schengen state (either); the law allows four months for a decision (the average is closer to two; four kept); the first permit costs 600 euros and a renewal 150 euros a year; it is 'generally renewed annually', read as a one-year term. Self-employment: a residence permit on the basis of self-employment, after an employment licence asked of Jobsplus, costs 100 euros the first time and 100 euros a year on renewal; a three-year period may be asked at renewal, so the first term is read as one year; where it is applied for isn't stated ('either' is the game's reading). EU nationals need no permit to reside and work in Malta, and EEA nationals have the right to reside when exercising treaty rights (Directive 2004/38, the Free Movement Order of 2007); Switzerland isn't named on the page and isn't kept. Long-term residence and whether these years count toward naturalisation (the Maltese Citizenship Act) aren't on the pages read and aren't kept.

sources.title: Identità, Single Permit
sources.said: The single permit is regulated by Subsidiary Legislation 217.17. It is a temporary-type permit which authorises third country nationals to legally reside and take up employment in Malta for a defined period of over 6 months which may be further renewed. ... an application may be submitted when the third-country national is either still abroad, that is, outside the Schengen area or when legally staying in the Maltese territory or another Schengen state. ... carry out paid duties assigned by parties other than the identified employer;

sources.title: Identità, Single Permit: Application Processing Period
sources.said: Subsidiary Legislation 217.17 allows four (4) months for the processing of a Single Permit application, however the average processing time is closer to two (2) months

sources.title: Identità, Single Permit: Applying for a Single Permit
sources.said: First time Single Permit: €600 ... Single Permit Renewal: €150 (per year)

sources.title: Identità, Single Permit: Renewal
sources.said: The single permit is generally renewed annually, and the administrative process follows the same single permit procedure.

sources.title: Identità, Employment/Self Employment
sources.said: Before submitting an Application for a Residence Permit on the basis of Self- Employment, an application with Jobsplus should have been submitted for a request to obtain an Employment Licence ... First-time applications €100 ... Renewal applications €100 per year for the duration of the permit (up to three years) ... At the renewal stage a request for a 3-year period may be submitted if the Employment licence covers such period.

sources.title: Identità, EU Nationals
sources.said: EU Nationals do not need a permit to reside and work in Malta. ... European Economic Area (EEA) nationals have the right to reside in Malta when exercising their treaty rights as workers, self-employed persons, economically self-sufficient persons
